items.title: Cluster sampling units, cluster totals, and one-stage SRSWOR
items.statement: Defines a finite population partitioned into primary sampling units (PSUs), the secondary sampling units (SSUs) within each PSU, fixed PSU totals, one-stage cluster sampling, and the exact uniform SRSWOR law for selecting a fixed number of PSUs.
items.strategy: Definition: partition the finite SSU population into nonempty finite clusters; state the PSU and SSU roles, fixed values and totals, target, general one-stage design law, and the uniform fixed-size SRSWOR specialization.

items.title: Two-stage sampling laws and the expansion estimator
items.statement: Defines a first-stage probability design on PSUs and independent conditional second-stage designs on each selected PSU, all stage-specific first- and second-order inclusion probabilities, the within-PSU Horvitz–Thompson total, and the two-stage expansion estimator under positive first-order inclusion probabilities.
items.strategy: Definition: give the joint law as the first-stage mass times the product of the selected PSUs' second-stage masses; define each stage's inclusion probabilities and state the positivity needed for both expansion divisions.

items.title: Unbiasedness and variance of the SRSWOR cluster-total estimator
items.statement: For a fixed finite population partitioned into M≥2 PSUs with fixed totals T_i, a uniform SRSWOR sample of m PSUs, 1≤m≤M, gives the unbiased estimator M times the sample mean of the PSU totals, with design variance M²(1−m/M)S_T²/m, where S_T² is the finite-population variance of the M PSU totals.
items.strategy: Direct: count first- and second-order inclusion probabilities, derive the indicator covariance, use the fixed-size centering identity, and expand the estimator variance as a finite sum.

items.title: Equal-size cluster design effect under exchangeable within-cluster covariance
items.statement: For independent equal-size cluster vectors of size m_c≥2, common marginal variance σ²>0, common within-cluster correlation ρ, and a negligible finite-population correction, the variance ratio of the mean from k sampled whole clusters to an element SRS of the same nominal size km_c is 1+(m_c−1)ρ. In this model ρ=0 means no ICC inflation; the sampling variance remains σ²/(km_c)>0.
items.strategy: Direct: expand the variance of a cluster mean using the m_c diagonal variances and m_c(m_c−1) within-cluster covariances, use independence across sampled PSUs, compare with the no-FPC element-SRS variance, and divide.

items.title: Unbiasedness and variance decomposition for the two-stage expansion total
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the product two-stage sampling law, positive first-order inclusion probabilities at both stages, and a fixed finite population, the expansion estimator is design-unbiased for the total and its variance is the first-stage HT variance of the true PSU totals plus the expected within-PSU sampling variance. The formula uses the stage-specific first- and second-order inclusion probabilities and does not require positive pair-inclusion probabilities.
items.strategy: Direct: establish the second-stage conditional mean and variance for each PSU, apply the published conditional-variance decomposition under its AC hypothesis, use conditional independence across selected PSUs, and expand each stage's finite covariance sum.

items.title: A two-stage village-and-field sample
items.statement: For two villages with four fixed field values each, samples one village by SRSWOR and then two fields within it by SRSWOR; enumerates the twelve two-stage outcomes, expansion estimates, unbiased mean, and exact design variance.
items.strategy: Direct finite enumeration: write both stage laws and all twelve joint outcomes, compute each expansion estimate, then calculate the exact finite weighted mean and variance.

items.title: Average cluster size does not determine the unequal-size design effect
items.statement: Refutes the proposed extension that the equal-size formula 1+(m_c−1)ρ remains valid after substituting the arithmetic mean cluster size when cluster sizes are unequal; half the clusters of size 1 and half of size 3 with a common random intercept give an ICC of 1, average size 2, but model-averaged finite-design variance ratio tending to 5/2 rather than 2.
items.strategy: Counterexample by exact model-averaged design variances: compute the between-PSU total variance and element-level finite-population variance for independent random intercepts, apply the two SRSWOR variance formulas at the same nominal sample size, and take the large-M, negligible-FPC limit.
